title: Probate & Trust Administration
subtitle: Navigating Probate & Trust Administration with Confidence

intro.text: The death of a loved one often brings legal and financial responsibilities at a time when families are already navigating significant change. Determining what must be done, what to prioritize, what deadlines apply, who has authority to act, and how assets should be handled can quickly become overwhelming.

AC Law Firm provides guidance throughout probate and trust administration. We work with Personal Representatives and Trustees to understand their responsibilities, navigate the administration process, and address the legal issues that may arise along the way.
Our goal is to bring clarity and structure to the process while helping fiduciaries fulfill their responsibilities and move the administration toward an appropriate resolution in a timely manner.

blocks.text: Probate is the court-supervised process through which a deceased person's estate may be administered. Depending on the circumstances, the process can involve identifying and valuing assets, addressing creditor claims, resolving outstanding obligations, preparing required filings and accountings, and ultimately distributing estate property to the appropriate beneficiaries or heirs.
AC Law Firm assists clients throughout the estate administration process, including:
Determining whether probate is necessary
Opening an estate
Petitioning for the appointment of a Personal Representative
Advising Personal Representatives regarding their fiduciary responsibilities
Identifying, collecting, and valuing estate assets
Preparing inventories and required probate filings
Addressing creditor claims and estate obligations
Coordinating appraisals and asset valuations
Assisting with the sale or transfer of estate property
Preparing fiduciary accountings
Communicating with beneficiaries and interested persons as requested
Addressing disputes or complications that arise during administration
Distributing estate assets
Closing the estate
Being named as a Personal Representative can carry significant responsibility.

A Personal Representative may be responsible for safeguarding estate property, identifying assets and debts, complying with court requirements, maintaining appropriate records, communicating with interested persons, resolving valid claims, and ensuring that distributions are made properly.
For many Personal Representatives, this is the first time they have been responsible for administering an estate.

AC Law Firm works closely with Personal Representatives throughout the process, helping them understand what is required, anticipate upcoming responsibilities, maintain appropriate documentation, and make informed decisions as issues arise.

A trustee's responsibilities often become more substantial after the death or incapacity of the person who created the trust. Even when trust assets do not pass through probate, administering a trust can involve significant legal, financial, and fiduciary obligations.
AC Law Firm assists trustees with understanding the governing trust documents and carrying out their responsibilities during administration.
Trust administration services may include:
Reviewing and interpreting trust documents
Advising successor trustees regarding their duties
Identifying and securing trust assets
Coordinating asset valuations
Reviewing ownership and beneficiary information
Assisting with required notices and communications
Addressing outstanding liabilities and expenses
Coordinating with accountants, financial institutions, and other professionals
Preparing or reviewing fiduciary accountings
Advising regarding distributions to beneficiaries
Addressing beneficiary questions and disputes
Assisting with the transfer or retitling of trust property
Guiding trustees through the completion of trust administration

Personal Representatives and trustees are fiduciaries. That role carries important responsibilities concerning the management, preservation, documentation, and distribution of assets belonging to an estate or trust.
Good recordkeeping is an essential part of that responsibility.
AC Law Firm assists fiduciaries with organizing and documenting financial activity, understanding accounting obligations, and preparing or reviewing fiduciary accountings when required.
When an estate or trust involves investment accounts, real property, business interests, significant transactions, or other complex assets, careful documentation can be particularly important.

sections.heading: When Probate and Trust Administration Overlap

blocks.text: An individual's estate plan may include both probate and non-probate assets. For example, some property may be owned by a trust while other assets remain individually titled and require probate administration.
When both an estate and trust must be administered, the Personal Representative and trustee may have separate—but sometimes overlapping—responsibilities.
AC Law Firm can help identify which assets belong to the estate, which are governed by a trust or beneficiary designation, and what administrative steps may be necessary for each.
Do all estates have to go through probate?

No. Whether probate is necessary depends on how the deceased person's assets were owned, the value and nature of those assets, beneficiary designations, and other circumstances. Some assets may transfer outside of probate even when a probate estate must be opened for other property.
What does a Personal Representative do?

A Personal Representative is responsible for administering the probate estate. Responsibilities may include locating and protecting assets, addressing debts and creditor claims, complying with court requirements, maintaining financial records, communicating with interested persons, and distributing estate property.
Does having a trust mean there is no administration after death?

No. A trust may allow properly titled assets to avoid probate, but the trust itself generally still requires administration. The successor trustee may need to identify assets, address expenses and liabilities, communicate with beneficiaries, maintain records, and ultimately distribute or continue managing trust property according to the trust's terms.
How long does estate or trust administration take?

There is no single timeline. The length of administration can depend on the nature and value of the assets, creditor issues, tax matters, property sales, beneficiary disputes, court requirements, and other circumstances. More complex estates and trusts may require substantially more time to administer properly.
What if beneficiaries and the Personal Representative or Trustee disagree?

Disagreements can arise regarding distributions, property, accountings, communications, fiduciary decisions, or the interpretation of estate planning documents. Addressing concerns early may help prevent disagreements from developing into more significant disputes. When necessary, legal counsel can assist with determining the fiduciary's obligations and available options.

sections.heading: Clear Guidance From Administration to Distribution

blocks.text: Probate and trust administration can involve much more than completing forms. Fiduciaries are often required to make important decisions while balancing legal obligations, financial considerations, deadlines, and family dynamics.

AC Law Firm provides practical legal guidance throughout the administration process so that Personal Representatives and trustees understand their responsibilities, the decisions before them, and the steps necessary to move the matter forward.

Whether you are preparing to open an estate, have already been appointed as Personal Representative, are beginning your responsibilities as successor trustee, or have encountered complications during administration, we can help you determine the appropriate next steps.

title: Business & Trademark Services
subtitle: Build With Intention. Protect What You Create.

intro.text: Building a business involves more than developing a great idea. The decisions made at the beginning—and as the business grows—can affect ownership, liability, operations, relationships, and the value of the brand you are creating.

AC Law Firm provides legal guidance to entrepreneurs and business owners seeking to establish a strong legal foundation for their businesses and protect the names, brands, and other intellectual property that distinguish them in the marketplace.

blocks.text: Choosing how to structure a business is an important early decision. The appropriate structure can depend on ownership, liability considerations, management, growth plans, and other business objectives.
AC Law Firm assists entrepreneurs and business owners with matters that may include:
Business formation
Limited Liability Company (LLC) formation
Entity selection
Formation and organizational documents
Operating agreements
Business agreements and contracts
Ownership and management considerations
Business changes and restructuring
General business legal guidance
Our goal is to help clients understand not only what documents are needed, but how the decisions reflected in those documents may affect the business moving forward.

Your business name, logo, slogan, or other brand identifiers can become valuable business assets. Trademark protection can help businesses establish and protect rights associated with the brands consumers use to identify their goods and services.

Trademark strategy
Preliminary trademark searches and evaluations
Federal trademark applications
Responses to certain USPTO correspondence
Trademark renewals and maintenance
Ownership changes and assignments
Portfolio guidance
General trademark counseling

sections.heading: Business Name, LLC, and Trademark: Understanding the Difference

blocks.text: Registering a business entity and obtaining trademark protection serve different purposes.

Forming an LLC or other business entity establishes the legal structure through which a business operates. Registering a business name with a state does not necessarily provide the same rights or protections associated with a federally registered trademark.
Trademark law focuses on the use of names, logos, and other identifiers as sources of particular goods or services.
Understanding the distinction early can help business owners make more informed decisions before investing substantial time and resources into developing a brand.

sections.heading: Protecting a Brand From the Beginning

blocks.text: Trademark considerations should not necessarily begin after a business becomes successful.

Before investing heavily in a business name, website, signage, packaging, marketing materials, or advertising, it can be valuable to consider whether the proposed brand may conflict with existing trademark rights and whether the name is capable of receiving meaningful protection.
Addressing these questions early can help businesses make more informed branding decisions and potentially avoid expensive changes later.
Do I need an LLC to start a business?

Not every business is legally required to operate as an LLC. Whether an LLC or another structure is appropriate depends on the nature of the business, ownership structure, liability concerns, and other considerations.
Does forming an LLC protect my business name as a trademark?

Not necessarily. Business formation and trademark protection are separate legal concepts. Approval of an entity name does not automatically establish federal trademark registration or mean that use of the name cannot conflict with another party's trademark rights.
When should I consider trademark protection?
Ideally, trademark considerations should arise relatively early in the branding process—particularly before making significant investments in a name or brand.
Can I trademark my business name?

Potentially. Whether a name is eligible for registration depends on several factors, including how the name is used, the goods or services associated with it, the distinctiveness of the mark, and existing trademark rights.

title: Estate Planning
subtitle: Gain Clarity For Your Future. Protect What Matters.

intro.text: Estate planning is about more than deciding what happens to your assets after your death. A thoughtful estate plan can help protect the people you care about, provide guidance during periods of incapacity, and ensure that important financial and healthcare decisions are made according to your wishes.

At AC Law Firm, we help individuals and families create estate plans tailored to their lives, priorities, and goals. Whether you are creating your first estate plan, experiencing a major life change, or reviewing documents you prepared years ago, we provide clear, practical guidance throughout the process.

blocks.text: Depending on your circumstances and objectives, your estate plan may include:
Last Will and Testament

A will allows you to direct how certain assets should be distributed after your death, nominate a Personal Representative to administer your estate, and address other important matters, including the nomination of guardians for minor children.
Revocable Living Trusts

A revocable living trust can provide a structured way to manage and transfer assets during your lifetime and after your death. Trust planning may also help with incapacity planning, privacy, and avoiding probate for assets that are properly transferred to the trust.
Powers of Attorney

A financial power of attorney allows you to designate someone you trust to handle financial and legal matters on your behalf if circumstances arise in which you are unable—or unavailable—to handle them yourself.
Advance Medical Directives
An advance medical directive allows you to communicate your healthcare preferences and designate an individual to make healthcare decisions on your behalf when necessary.
Estate Plan Reviews and Updates

Estate plans should evolve as your life changes. Marriage, divorce, the birth of a child, the purchase of property, changes in financial circumstances, relocation, or the death of a loved one may create a reason to revisit your existing plan.

sections.heading: Who Should Have an Estate Plan?

blocks.text: Estate planning is not reserved for individuals with significant wealth. If you own property, have financial accounts, have children or other loved ones you want to protect, own a business, or simply want greater control over future financial and healthcare decisions, an estate plan can provide important protections.
Planning can be particularly important after major life events such as:
Marriage or divorce
Having or adopting a child
Purchasing a home
Starting or acquiring a business
Accumulating significant assets
Moving to a new state
Changes in family relationships
Receiving an inheritance
A significant change in health or circumstances

sections.heading: A Plan Designed Around Your Life

blocks.text: No two families are exactly alike, and an estate plan should reflect more than a collection of standard documents.

Our process begins with understanding your family, your assets, your concerns, and what you want your plan to accomplish. From there, we identify the planning tools appropriate for your circumstances and explain your options in straightforward terms so that you can make informed decisions.
The goal is not simply to prepare documents. It is to create a coordinated plan that reflects your wishes and provides clear direction when it matters most.
Do I need both a will and a trust?

Not everyone needs a trust, and having a trust does not necessarily eliminate the need for a will. The appropriate combination of documents depends on your assets, family circumstances, planning objectives, and how you want those assets managed and transferred.
Can an estate plan help avoid probate?

Certain planning strategies may allow assets to pass outside of probate, including properly funded trusts, beneficiary designations, and certain forms of joint ownership. Whether avoiding probate should be a primary objective depends on your individual circumstances.
When should I update my estate plan?

You should consider reviewing your estate plan after significant life or financial changes. Even without a major event, periodically reviewing your documents can help ensure that your fiduciary appointments, beneficiary choices, and planning objectives continue to reflect your wishes.
What happens if I become incapacitated?

A comprehensive estate plan can designate trusted individuals to assist with financial and healthcare decisions if you are unable to make or communicate those decisions yourself. Planning in advance can reduce uncertainty for both you and your family.

You do not need to have every answer before speaking with an estate planning attorney. Part of the planning process is identifying the questions that need to be considered and understanding the options available to you.
AC Law Firm provides personalized estate planning counsel designed to help you make informed decisions, protect the people and interests that matter to you, and move forward with greater clarity.

title: Guardianships
subtitle: Protecting the Interests of Those Who Need Support

intro.text: When an individual is unable to make certain personal, medical, or financial decisions independently, a guardianship may provide the legal authority necessary for another person to act on their behalf.

Guardianship proceedings can involve deeply personal circumstances, significant responsibilities, and important questions about an individual's independence and well-being. AC Law Firm helps individuals and families understand the guardianship process, evaluate available options, and navigate the legal responsibilities that may follow.

blocks.text: AC Law Firm provides guidance in guardianship matters that may include:
Petitions for guardianship
Adult guardianships
Guardianships involving minors, when applicable
Guardianship of the person
Guardianship of property
Emergency guardianship matters
Advising proposed and appointed guardians
Required court filings and reports
Fiduciary responsibilities and accountings
Modification or termination of guardianships
Contested guardianship matters

Guardianship may become necessary when an individual is unable to adequately manage certain personal, medical, or financial matters and there is no less restrictive arrangement that sufficiently addresses those needs.
These circumstances can arise because of incapacity, illness, injury, disability, age, or other circumstances affecting an individual's ability to make or communicate decisions.

Because guardianship can significantly affect an individual's rights and independence, courts generally consider both the need for guardianship and whether less restrictive alternatives are available.

sections.heading: Guardianship of the Person and Guardianship of Property

blocks.text: Depending on the circumstances, a court may appoint a guardian to make decisions concerning an individual's personal affairs, financial affairs, or both.
A guardian of the person may be authorized to make certain decisions concerning healthcare, living arrangements, personal care, and other matters affecting the individual's well-being.
A guardian of property may be responsible for managing assets, income, expenses, and other financial matters on behalf of the individual.
The authority and responsibilities of a guardian depend on the court's order and applicable law.
Being appointed guardian is not simply an authorization to act. It creates ongoing legal and fiduciary responsibilities.

Depending on the type of guardianship, a guardian may be required to safeguard property, maintain financial records, make decisions in the protected person's interests, submit reports or accountings, obtain court approval for certain actions, and comply with continuing court oversight.
AC Law Firm assists guardians in understanding these responsibilities and navigating the requirements that continue after appointment.
Is guardianship always necessary when someone becomes incapacitated?

No. Powers of attorney, advance directives, trusts, supported decision-making arrangements, or other alternatives may provide sufficient authority in some circumstances. Whether guardianship is necessary depends on the individual's circumstances and what planning is already in place.
Who can petition for guardianship?

Eligibility and procedural requirements depend on the type of guardianship and applicable law. A family member or another interested person may be able to initiate proceedings when circumstances warrant court intervention.
Does a guardian have complete control over another person's affairs?
Not necessarily. A guardian's authority is defined by applicable law and the court's order. The scope of a guardianship should correspond to the authority necessary under the circumstances.
Is a guardian required to report to the court?
Guardianships generally involve continuing court oversight. Depending on the type of appointment, guardians may have reporting, recordkeeping, accounting, or other ongoing obligations.

Guardianship matters require careful consideration of both legal responsibilities and the needs of the individual involved. AC Law Firm provides practical guidance to help clients understand the process, evaluate their options, and fulfill the responsibilities associated with guardianship.

title: Marital Agreements
subtitle: Thoughtful Planning for the Life You're Building Together

intro.text: Conversations about finances, property, and future responsibilities are an important part of planning a life together. A marital agreement provides couples with an opportunity to have those conversations intentionally and establish clear expectations regarding certain financial matters.
AC Law Firm assists individuals with the preparation and review of prenuptial and postnuptial agreements designed to reflect their circumstances, priorities, and objectives.

A marital agreement is not simply about preparing for the end of a marriage. It can be a planning tool that promotes transparency, clarifies expectations, and allows couples to make important financial decisions for themselves.

blocks.text: A prenuptial agreement is entered into before marriage and can address certain financial and property rights between prospective spouses.
Depending on the circumstances and applicable law, a prenuptial agreement may address matters such as:
Property owned before the marriage
Treatment of property acquired during the marriage
Business interests
Investments and financial accounts
Debts and financial obligations
Inheritances and family assets
Rights concerning certain property upon separation, divorce, or death
Spousal support considerations
Other financial rights and responsibilities
The appropriate provisions depend on each couple's circumstances and objectives.
Couples may also decide to establish financial agreements after they are already married.
A postnuptial agreement can address many of the same financial considerations as a prenuptial agreement but is entered into during the marriage.

A couple might consider a postnuptial agreement after a significant change in financial circumstances, the creation or growth of a business, receipt of an inheritance, changes in family responsibilities, or simply because they would like greater clarity regarding their financial arrangements.
Marriage creates financial and legal rights that can also affect estate planning.

For individuals entering a marriage with children from a previous relationship, significant separate property, family assets, business interests, or specific inheritance objectives, coordinating a marital agreement with an estate plan can be particularly important.
A well-considered planning process looks at how these documents interact rather than treating them as entirely separate matters.
Discussing a prenuptial or postnuptial agreement can feel uncomfortable, but the process can also encourage meaningful conversations about finances, expectations, property, debt, and long-term goals.

Beginning the process early provides both individuals with time to consider the proposed terms, obtain independent legal advice when appropriate, exchange relevant financial information, and make informed decisions without unnecessary time pressure.
Who should consider a prenuptial agreement?

Prenuptial agreements are not limited to individuals with substantial wealth. They may be worth considering when either person owns a business, has significant assets or debts, expects an inheritance, has children from a prior relationship, owns real estate, or simply wants greater clarity concerning financial rights and responsibilities.
Can we create an agreement after we're already married?
Potentially. A postnuptial agreement is entered into after marriage and may address certain property and financial matters between spouses.
Does asking for a prenup mean you expect the marriage to fail?

A marital agreement does not have to be approached that way. For many couples, it is a form of financial planning that allows them to discuss expectations and decide in advance how certain financial matters should be treated.
Can one attorney represent both people?

Because each person may have separate legal interests concerning the agreement, independent legal representation can be important. AC Law Firm can explain the appropriate representation structure based on the circumstances.
When should we start the prenuptial agreement process?

Starting well in advance of the wedding is preferable. This provides time for financial disclosure, negotiation, review, independent legal advice where appropriate, and thoughtful decision-making without the pressure of an approaching wedding date.

sections.heading: Plan the Marriage, Not Just the Wedding

blocks.text: Marriage is both a personal commitment and a relationship with significant legal and financial consequences. Thoughtful planning allows couples to address those realities openly and establish expectations that reflect their circumstances.
